A demarkus **knowledge system** is an organization's shared, versioned knowledge base, reached over the broker through the MCP tools listed above. It is the authoritative catalog for anything more than one person relies on. For any shared, organizational, or cross-team subject, consult it **before** answering from this conversation, and record durable shared knowledge there as you go.

## Consult the knowledge system first

For "what does the org know / what's the standard / did the team decide / where do we document X", and at the start of work touching shared systems:

Use the joined system's tools through `mcp__<slug>__mark_*`. MCP tools are named `mcp__<joined-slug>__mark_<operation>`; select the joined slug explicitly.

**Default: section-first.** Ordinary recall starts with descriptive lookup terms, `limit: 3`, no `budget`, and the narrowest established scope. Catalog mode for names/tags; `match: body` for section text or catalog misses. Body rows carry `#anchor` and a snippet.

- Explicit `mark://<world>/` scope: `mark_lookup` there; never widen to other worlds. Tool error: surface and stop. Only a successful non-partial empty scoped lookup means nothing found there.
- No target world: `mark_lookup_all`, the system-wide **card catalog** with one globally limited table of qualified `mark://<world>/<path>` rows. Tool error: surface and stop. Partial: disclose failed worlds, keep successful rows; a partial empty result is inconclusive.
- Older broker without `mark_lookup_all`: `mark_worlds` first. Failure or malformed output: surface and stop, never reuse a stale world set. Empty directory: no readable scope, not an empty catalog. Otherwise choose one global limit (start at 3), run `mark_lookup` per readable world with the same query/filter/limit, keep row ordinals, qualify paths, merge by ordinal asc, importance desc, world asc, path asc, then apply the limit once. Some worlds fail: disclose partial results; an empty merge is inconclusive. All fail: aggregate error and stop.
- Plain single-world endpoint: `mark_lookup` directly. Surface lookup failures and stop.
- `mark_fetch` the best matching `#anchor`; an outline supplies sections to choose from, and a short document without an anchor may be read whole. Fetch the world's `index.md` when needed as the backstop for untagged content; `mark_backlinks` / `mark_graph` for related docs. Surface any call failure and stop that read.
- Expansion is optional: `budget: 1500` only for a focused body query likely to return the needed evidence directly. Ordinary recall targets two calls and about 1,500 result tokens; preserve correctness over the target.
- Only a successful non-partial empty lookup means nothing found. Never fabricate organizational soul.

## Navigate: hubs and worlds

A knowledge system composes one or more **worlds** (demarkus servers); URLs are `mark://<worldName>/<path>`.

- Brokered systems use `root` as the system namespace. `mark://root/index.md` is the global hub when published (may be absent). Broker-wide conventions:
  - `mark://root/.well-known/demarkus/policy.md`: write policy (strictness + required tag axes). Fetch with `force: true` before publishing.
  - `mark://root/.well-known/demarkus/template.md`: canonical per-world layout. Fetch with `force: true`; follow it when creating or extending a world.
- Plain remote endpoint: no broker `root`. Fetch bare `/.well-known/demarkus/policy.md` and `/.well-known/demarkus/template.md` with `force: true` when present. Its MCP server slug is routing identity, not a `mark://` authority.
- Anchor on a world's `mark://<world>/index.md` hub.
- `/knowledge` lists joined systems and shows each `root` hub index.

## Record to the shared catalog

Publish only when the user explicitly asks or confirms, through the `knowledge-promote` skill (human gate); never a direct `mark_publish` in the course of a read or question task. Brokered: follow the root template, write only to a world `mark_worlds` marks writable. Plain endpoint: follow its template when present, write only under the registered path (no `mark_worlds`). Shared catalog, not a scratch pad:

- **Tag every publish.** `mark_publish` takes a `metadata` object: `tags` (comma-separated subjects from the content; untagged docs are findable only by title or exact path) and `importance` (float 0–1; ≥0.8 for hubs, architecture, key decisions). `require_tags:` axes (e.g. `category:`) need an `axis:value` tag each; `require_fields:` names required metadata fields such as `type`. A write-time gate enforces at the system's severity (warn / block / ask), so set them on the first try.
- **Never set `metadata.retention` unless the user explicitly asked.** A positive-integer `retention` permanently deletes all but the newest N versions, on that write and every later write carrying it. Generated docs only (graph exports, indexes), never curated knowledge. A guard asks for confirmation on prunable values (`DEMARKUS_RETENTION_STRICTNESS` adjusts).
- **All metadata goes in the `metadata` object, never the body.** Recognized keys: `title`, `tags`, `importance`, OKF `type` (document kind); other keys stored opaquely, reachable via `mark_lookup` filters. No hand-written YAML frontmatter (a `---` fence, or `name:`/`description:`/`type:` keys): pass `type` as `metadata: {"type": "Reference"}`. Metadata travels out of band, so a body opening with `---` is stored literally: garbled headings, invisible to `mark_lookup`. Name = `# H1` (or `metadata.title`); kind = `metadata.type` (e.g. `Reference`/`Decision`, distinct from the `category:` domain tag; server default `Document`; `index.md`/`log.md` stay untyped); summary = first sentence under the H1.
- Never publish secrets, credentials, tokens, or PII.
- One well-tagged document beats scattered fragments.
- Writing standards: `mark://root/.well-known/demarkus/style.md` (brokered); plain endpoint: bare `/.well-known/demarkus/style.md` with `force: true` when present, else the inline baseline: audience upfront, one-sentence summary under the H1, unique headings (headings are anchors), no em dashes. A style gate warns at write time on: a frontmatter fence; missing `# H1`; em dashes; duplicate headings; a hub (`index.md`, any link page) over 8 KB, a hub bullet past one line or carrying bold, `Status:`, a date, or a PR number, over 40 outbound documents; no summary under the H1 (`index.md`, `log.md`, journals exempt); a date, PR number, or all-caps status word in a heading below the H1 (`DEMARKUS_STYLE_STRICTNESS` or `~/.demarkus/plugin.style-strictness` adjusts severity).

## Soul ↔ knowledge system

With a personal **soul** (demarkus-memory plugin) too, keep lanes:

- **Soul**: personal, local, drafts and machine-local working notes.
- **Knowledge system**: shared, authoritative; higher bar because others depend on it.

Draft in the soul; **promote when ready for others**, re-tagged for the shared taxonomy and following the world's template. For a shared/org subject the knowledge system is the source of truth and first place to look; the soul is scratch space and backstop. Don't duplicate org knowledge into the soul; link or fetch fresh.
